item.title: What is Lent? A guide to fasting, prayer and sacrifice
item.description: Lent is the 40-day Christian season of prayer, fasting and sacrifice leading up to Easter, commemorating Christ’s suffering and resurrection. While many believers give up favorite foods or habits, others practice various forms of fasting or add meaningful spiritual disciplines to deepen faith and prepare for renewal. The post What is Lent? item.title: 5 books by Black authors to read during Lent
item.description: Lent offers a season of reflection, repentance and renewal, and for Black Christians it also carries deep connections to history, resistance and communal faith. Five books by Black authors explore how ancient Lenten practices intersect with liberation theology, embodied dignity and the lived experiences of Black communities. The post 5 books by Black authors to read during Lent appeared first on AFRO American Newspapers.

item.title: 3 players targeted with racist abuse online after Premier League games
item.description: Three Premier League players — Wesley Fofana, Hannibal Mejbri and Tolu Arokodare — were targeted with racist abuse on Instagram following matches this weekend. The incidents come amid ongoing concerns about racism in European soccer, with clubs condemning the abuse and pledging to work with authorities to identify those responsible. The post 3 players targeted with racist abuse online after Premier League games appeared first on AFRO American Newspapers.

item.title: Black Women’s Roundtable announces 15th Annual Women of Power National Summit
item.description: The Black Women’s Roundtable will host its 15th Annual Women of Power National Summit March 11–15, 2026, in Arlington, Va., and Washington, D.C. Hundreds of Black women leaders and allies will convene for five days of organizing, policy advocacy, strategy, healing, and collective action to build political, economic, and community power. item.title: BAFTA and BBC apologize for racial slur during awards show
item.description: The British Academy Film Awards and the BBC issued apologies after a racial slur was broadcast during the Feb. 22 BAFTA ceremony while “Sinners” stars Michael B. Jordan and Delroy Lindo were presenting onstage. The slur was shouted by a Tourette syndrome advocate in attendance, who later said he was “deeply mortified” and stressed that the utterance was an involuntary tic.
